newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African HIV rate up 35 pct among pregnant women.
newsitem.headline: S.African HIV rate up 35 pct among pregnant women.

text.p: South Africa's HIV infection rate rose 34.8 percent in 1996 to 14.07 percent of all pregnant women tested, the government said in survey results published on Wednesday.
Anonymous testing of more than 15,000 pregnant women attending state hospitals showed the infection rate up from 10.44 percent at the end of 1995 to 14.07 last year.
HIV is the virus that causes the fatal acquired immune deficiency syndrome, AIDS.
Infections have almost doubled from 7.57 percent in 1994.
"The sharp increase of 34.8 percent over the previous year confirms that South Africa is still experiencing a fast growing HIV epidemic," the Health Ministry said in a report on the survey.
The highest infection rate and a threefold increase was recorded in Northwest Province, near Johannesburg, where positive tests jumped from 8.3 percent in 1995 to 25.13 percent last year.
KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's most populous province and previously the worst affected, showed a modest increase from 18.23 percent to 19.9 percent last year.
The Western Cape, which includes Cape Town, showed the lowest infection rate of 1.65 percent, which was unchanged from the previous year.
